H6AZ01322.name: David Redkey
H6AZ01322.bio: Certified teacher who has lived in Arizona for nearly four decades.

positions.stance: Calls Section 219 of the 2027 NDAA "nothing less than treason," saying it allows Israel to gain access to U.S. weapon systems.
Supports FDR's Economic Bill of Rights, including rights to a living-wage job, a decent home, medical care, and a good education.
Proposes "TriCare Prime for All," a single-payer universal system modeled on TRICARE Prime with "No co-pays. No deductibles. No medical bills."
Proposes a 94% marginal rate on income above $200,000 (single) or $400,000 (joint), paired with tax credits for employers paying living wages.
Supports "immediate recognition and publication of the Equal Rights Amendment as the 28th Amendment" and removing the ratification deadline.

wiki:tisha-benoit.name: Tisha Benoit
wiki:tisha-benoit.bio: Has spent much of her professional life in healthcare.

positions.stance: Wants to stop policies that raise costs, make it easier to start small businesses, and tie workforce training to actual jobs.
Wants to increase housing supply by reducing barriers, encouraging starter homes, and adding transparency on institutional investors buying single-family homes.
Supports conservation plus "an aggressive water innovation strategy" and an all-of-the-above energy mix while keeping energy bills affordable.
Supports border security with personnel, technology and barriers where effective, plus faster immigration courts and a modern legal immigration system.
Supports reform centered on price transparency, competition, prevention, and patient choice, not "government-run healthcare or corporate-run healthcare."
Supports reducing the military budget by 90%, closing all foreign military bases, and abolishing nuclear weapons.
Says Israel has committed genocide against Gaza; supports war crimes tribunals, reparations, and nonviolent conflict resolution.
Supports electing Congress by proportional representation, abolishing the Senate and Electoral College, and adopting a parliamentary system.
Supports impeaching and convicting "Trump, Vance, and their entire cabinet."
Supports national initiative and referendum, public campaign financing, campaign spending limits, and easy ballot access.

H4MA01091.name: Nadia Milleron
H4MA01091.bio: Farmer and attorney who ran for this seat in 2024.

positions.stance: Supports eliminating the federal income tax on earnings under $100,000.
Will fight for Social Security "and to bring benefits up to today's standard of living."
Supports keeping corporations out of politics and a federal charter for large corporations requiring transparency, accountability, and fair taxation.
Supports an economic job guarantee and will vote against sending taxpayer money to fund foreign wars.
Will work to rebuild American manufacturing with strong labor and environmental standards, including making medicine at home.

H6MA08372.name: Rasheed Nicholas Walters
H6MA08372.bio: Businessman, media professional, and former Boston Herald opinion writer.

positions.stance: Would redirect federal transportation funding from new bike and bus lane projects toward road repair, and create direct federal pothole grants to towns.
Will request a full federal forensic audit of pandemic and relief funding flowing through Massachusetts.
Would introduce legislation "eliminating all federal transportation dollars for bicycle-lane and bus-lane projects" and audit bike lanes for ADA compliance.
Would require employers to pay undocumented workers equal wages plus a tax, and eliminate visa programs that replace American workers.
Opposes the MBTA Communities Act and pledges to defend suburban communities' right to local zoning control.

wiki:chris-campbell.name: Chris Campbell
wiki:chris-campbell.bio: Mechanical engineer who has worked in manufacturing in Tennessee and Southwestern Virginia.

positions.stance: Would eliminate the cap on income subject to FICA tax while keeping the benefit cap, and wants a CBO study of the system's finances.
Says "If it is considered compensation, then it is income," seeking to tax executive compensation held as unrealized wealth.
Supports a sliding-scale insurance program, limits on selling medical debt, and expanding HSAs to pay premiums before Medicare.
Says "responsible manufacturing companies make for financially strong communities" and wants East Tennessee to regain manufacturing jobs.
Supports small businesses and bringing good-paying jobs to East Tennessee.
Supports making healthcare more affordable, protecting coverage for pre-existing conditions, and lowering prescription drug costs.
Supports honoring veterans "with the benefits they've earned" and ensuring service members have the support they need.
Supports investing in public schools, supporting teachers, and expanding vocational training and community college opportunities.
Supports term limits, campaign finance reform, and "ending the revolving door between Congress and lobbyists."

H6TN02188.name: Adam Heimerman
H6TN02188.bio: River guide and seventh-generation East Tennessean.

positions.stance: Supports secure borders with a compassionate legal route of immigration, protecting genuine asylum seekers, and cracking down on trafficking.
Would introduce legislation to overturn Citizens United and ban corporate Super PAC contributions; "Corporations are not people."
Supports federal affordable housing grants, restricting institutional bulk-buying of single-family homes, and more first-time homebuyer assistance.
Says "clean water, clean air, and protected public lands are not political issues — they are survival issues."
Calls the debt "a policy failure," favoring domestic investment over "senseless campaigns of military destruction" and corporate subsidies.

H6TN03251.name: Rodney Joe King
H6TN03251.bio: Retired U.S. Navy officer and former public school science teacher.

positions.stance: Calls himself "an unapologetic environmentalist" and says Earth's resources should be used with common sense and best practices.
States: "I believe in the 'Right to Life'."
States: "I support the second amendment."
Supports saving Social Security, saying the wealthy who received tax breaks should now pay what was negotiated.
Supports universal health care, saying the country "can afford to supply the people with health care."

H6TN04242.name: Jacob Anders
H6TN04242.bio: Author, historian, and digital ethics researcher; former Marion County commissioner.

positions.stance: Supports a constitutional amendment limiting House members to three terms and senators to two terms.
Would eliminate the Social Security tax cap and "stand against any attempt to cut or privatize" benefits.
Supports a full ban on members of Congress, their spouses, and children trading individual stocks.
Would fight to repeal the USA PATRIOT Act and the Authorizations for Use of Military Force, and regulate or ban mass surveillance technology.
Supports repealing the Permanent Apportionment Act of 1929 and expanding the House before the 2030 census.

wiki:angus-purdy.name: Angus Purdy
wiki:angus-purdy.bio: Vanderbilt graduate who works at Little Hats Italian Market in Hillsboro Village.

positions.stance: Wants to "return to tax rates that force the ultra wealthy to pay their fair share."
Wants to limit executive privilege and "put declarations of war and military spending back in the hands of Congress."
Calls the DOJ's "anti-weaponization" fund a misuse of taxpayer dollars and wants officials held criminally liable for corruption.
Supports farm subsidies, universal basic income, rural hospitals, public education, rent control, and affordable childcare.
Says Social Security "is not a government handout; it is a system we all pay into, collectively."

H6TN05330.name: Lowell Reynolds
H6TN05330.bio: Grammy-winning music industry engineer and law student at Syracuse University College of Law.
